title: Sound
examples: What makes a sound happen in the first place?
How does the speed of sound change in different materials?
If I hear an echo, how can I figure out how far away it was?

explain.say: Sound starts with something that is vibrating really fast.
The vibrations create waves that travel through the air to your ear.
Pitch is determined by how fast the vibrations are happening.
Loudness depends on how big the vibrations are getting.
An echo is just a sound wave bouncing off a hard surface.
The speed of sound is quite constant in dry air at room temperature.

draw.text: Sound speed in air is constant.

faq.q: How does the speed of sound change in water compared to air?
faq.a: Sound travels much faster in water than it does through the air. This is because water is a denser medium.
asks: Does the speed change in liquids?

faq.q: If I clap my hands, what causes the echo I hear later?
faq.a: The sound wave travels to the wall and bounces back to you. That returning wave is what you hear as an echo.
asks: Where does the echo come from?
What is the reflection of sound?

faq.q: Does the pitch tell me anything about how loud the sound is?
faq.a: No, pitch and loudness are different properties. Pitch relates to frequency, and loudness relates to amplitude.
asks: Are pitch and volume the same thing?
What is the difference between pitch and amplitude?

faq.q: Why is sound not heard in space?
faq.a: Sound needs a medium, like air or water, to travel. Space is a vacuum, so there are no particles to vibrate.
asks: Can sound travel in a vacuum?

faq.q: What determines if a sound is high or low pitched?
faq.a: The pitch is determined by the frequency of the vibrations, which is how many vibrations happen per second.

facts: Sound travels as a mechanical wave, meaning it needs a medium.
Pitch is related to the frequency of the vibrations.
Loudness is related to the amplitude of the vibrations.
The speed of sound is fastest in solids, then liquids, and slowest in gases.

quiz.say: A very low, deep note from a tuba has a:
quiz.why: Low frequency means the vibrations are happening slowly, which we perceive as a low pitch.

wrong.1: Low amplitude means the sound is quiet, not necessarily low pitched.
wrong.2: The speed of sound is not changed by the pitch of the sound.
wrong.3: Energy relates more to loudness, not directly to the pitch.

quiz.say: If you measure the time for an echo, what physical property are you calculating?
quiz.why: The time taken for the sound to go out and bounce back allows you to calculate the total distance traveled.

wrong.0: You need the time and speed to find the distance, not the other way around.
wrong.1: Echo time tells you about distance, not the pitch of the original sound.
wrong.2: Loudness is about the energy, not the time taken for the reflection.

quiz.say: When sound travels from air into a solid metal bar, what happens to its speed?
quiz.why: Sound travels faster in denser and more rigid materials like metals compared to air.

wrong.0: Sound waves can pass through many different materials.
wrong.2: Sound generally speeds up when moving to a denser material.
wrong.3: The speed of sound changes depending on the material it passes through.
